newsitem.title: POLAND: Russia's Chernomyrdin to visit Poland.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Chernomyrdin to visit Poland.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will visit Poland next Thursday for the opening of a gas pipeline and to follow up last week's talks with his Polish counterpart, Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati said.

Rosati told a news conference on Thursday that Chernomyrdin, returning home from Bonn, would stop off for a few hours in Poznan, western Poland to attend an opening ceremony for a gas line to link Russia, Poland and Germany.

Chernomyrdin would hold talks with Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz who in Moscow last week signed a memorandum on future trade liberalisation between the two countries and an agreement on mutual visa-free travel.
"We are glad to be able to host him in our country and this is also evidence that relations are normal," Rosati said.
The dropping of visas has been long delayed because Moscow resisted Warsaw's precondition that it agree to readmit illegal immigrants who had crossed from Russian territory into Poland.
Rosati said Russia had come round and Chernomyrdin might sign the readmission deal while in Poznan, if the details had been readied by then, and visa-free travel could then start.
Poland's ties with Russia have been strained by its aim to enter the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation as fast as possible -- a move Moscow sees as a security threat.
Cimoszewicz's trip underlined that the two were still able to do business despite this fundamental difference.

Rosati said Russia was likely to present ill-defined ideas for an alternative European security model during a Lisbon summit of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) next month.

"These (ideas) are just thoughts and fragments, generally aimed at strengthening the OSCE and making it into a kind of counter-balance for NATO," said Rosati, whose country, having escaped Soviet domination in 1989, is set on full NATO entry.

"As there is no possibility for compromise in this area, I think this concept of security, which the Russians have proposed in the past, will not see the light of day as a comprehensive concept," he said.
